passage:
Zainab set the report card beside the dal. "Eighty-two? Last time it was ninety-one."
"It was a hard paper, Ammi."
"Board exams are in four months, Rehana."
Rehana stared at the rice. "I feel like you only smile when I score."
"That is not fair." Silence. Then, quieter: "I'm scared, beta. I never got to study past tenth. I don't want you to lose choices."
Rehana's shoulders dropped. "I hear that. But it helps when we make a weekly plan together. And when Friday nights are calm, with no marks talk."
"Friday nights, fine." Zainab slid the plate closer. "Plan tomorrow?"
"Okay, Ammi. Thank you."

qa.q: What marks did Rehana score, and what was the last score?
qa.a: Rehana scored eighty-two, and last time it was ninety-one.

qa.q: What does Rehana's staring at the rice suggest about how Rehana felt after the marks question?
qa.a: It suggests hurt and a pull to shut down, since Rehana then says "I feel like you only smile when I score."

qa.q: Which choice helped in this conversation, and why?
qa.a: Rehana listened to the fear behind the push and then asked for a weekly plan and calm Friday nights, so the talk turned from blame to a shared step.

qa.q: What is Ammi feeling underneath the push about marks?
qa.a: Fear that Rehana will lose choices; Ammi says "I'm scared" and mentions never getting to study past tenth. ❤️

grounding: Rehana feels measured by marks, hears the parent's fear behind the push and says what would help instead of shutting down.

passage:
Friday night

Mummy checked my unit test marks at the gate today before even saying hi. 72 in physics. Her face did the thing. "Only 72, Tarun? Sharma aunty's daughter got 90." Then silence all the way home.

When I get 90, she hugs me. When I get 72, she goes cold. Sometimes I think she only loves the marks.

I stayed in my room all evening and didn't come out for dinner. Then I heard her on the phone with Nani, and she said, "I just don't want him to struggle like I did. I never got to finish college." Her voice was shaking.

I didn't know that.

I went and sat next to her. I said, "Mummy, when you go quiet after marks, it feels like you stop loving me. What would help is if we made a study plan together on Sundays, and on other nights we just have dinner without talking about tests."

She hugged me for a long time. She said yes to the Sunday plan.

qa.q: What mark did Tarun get in physics?
What did Tarun feel when Mummy went quiet after seeing the marks?
qa.a: Tarun felt hurt and unloved, as if her love depended on his marks.

qa.q: What did Tarun ask for that could help both of them?
qa.a: Tarun asked for a Sunday study plan together and calm dinners on other nights without talk of tests.

qa.q: How might Mummy's own past shape the way she pushes Tarun?
qa.a: Having never finished college herself, she seems afraid he will struggle as she did, so her fear comes out as pressure.

grounding: It shows a teen who feels measured by marks and that love is conditional, who hears the fear behind the parent's push and says what helps instead of shutting down.

passage:
Mridul: my dad made a chart
Joseph: a chart??
Mridul: of every test mark since jan. on the fridge. with a red line for "target"
Joseph: bro 😬
Mridul: when i'm above the line he's all smiles. below it and he barely talks
Mridul: feels like i only matter when i'm above the line
Joseph: that sucks. have u told him?
Mridul: no. i just go to my room
Joseph: my mom was like that in class 10. turns out she was scared bc her brother failed boards and it wrecked him for years
Mridul: hmm. dad did say once he didn't want me to "end up like him at the factory"
Joseph: so maybe it's fear not just marks?
Mridul: maybe
Joseph: tell him what helps. like "check marks once a week not every day"
Mridul: or take the chart off the fridge lol
Joseph: start with once a week 😅
Mridul: ok. after dinner. wish me luck

qa.q: What is on the fridge in Mridul's house?
qa.a: A chart of every test mark since January, with a red line for "target", is on the fridge.

qa.q: What does Mridul feel when his dad barely talks after a low mark?
qa.a: Mridul feels hurt and unimportant, as if he only matters when he is above the line.

qa.q: Which suggestion from Joseph could help, and why?
qa.a: Asking his dad to check marks once a week could help, because it names a clear change that lowers pressure without shutting his father out.

qa.q: Why might Mridul's dad push so hard about marks?
qa.a: His dad seems afraid Mridul will end up stuck at a factory like him, so the push may come from fear more than lack of love.

grounding: It shows a teen who feels measured by marks and that love is conditional, who is helped to see the fear behind the push and to say what helps.
